# Parameterized object-body Java observations

This fixture contains independently acquired Pkl 0.32.0 Java results. It contains no Rust-derived expectations or compatibility verdict. Inputs are project-authored controls; copied project sources retain the repository license. The original upstream CLI input remains separately pinned by its unchanged corpus/source identities.

`cases.json` selects ordinary, reached semantics and complete language diagnostics. Each source has its original absolute URI and module name; consumers must use that URI rather than rewrite diagnostic bytes. Both fresh Java process observations are recorded. Identical ordinary stdout/stderr/outcome payloads are stored once; process records and original cohort hashes preserve both acquisitions. Raw output has no trimming, sorting, or reserialization. `inputs/*/gate.txt` is the exact file resource for the read controls.

`oracle-boundaries.json` retains two PklBugException inputs, two recursive receiver controls that produced Java StackOverflowError, and three forbidden for/when-body parameter inputs that produced Java MissingResourceException before the probe outcome could be written. These are oracle errors, even if a candidate prints the same bytes. Stack-overflow repeats may differ. `historical-observations.json` separates earlier equivalent dispatch/arity observations from syntax, reserved-name, and scalar-amendment controls whose intended behavior was not reached. These historical rows never add selected feature passes. Selected original reports, source/probe copies, commands, controlled environment, input identities and full selected raw payloads are preserved here. Earlier excluded acquisition raw files remain in the recorded historical target cohorts; their absence on another host does not alter the explicit unreached/superseded ledger.

`original-cli/` records two executions with the original corpus argv/cwd/environment overrides through `m2_module_eval.capture_process`. Both exited zero with empty stdout/stderr and no generated public files. Its all-local functions are not called, so that result alone does not establish Mixin semantics. A minimal input graph was sufficient for this all-local source; this packet is not a full upstream resource-set replay.

The scalar Java probe prints `evaluateExpressionString` output and a separate exception-class outcome. These API observations have no public file-output operation; the input/resource tree was unchanged before and after every cohort. They do not establish renderer, Host event-order, public API lifecycle, platform, language-wide, or performance compatibility. The controlled process environment and runtime identities are in `provenance/oracle.json`; every exact invocation is in its process record. The narrow repository verifier independently pins the Java authority reports, probe bytecode/source and runtime metadata. Run `python3 tools/parameterized_object_fixtures.py` to validate this fixture without ignored target directories or installed Java. The separate read cases require exact URI resources from their `resources` arrays. No Java logger/read callback trace was acquired by the plain scalar probe; native event-order/lifecycle tests have a separate scope.
